title: Materials
summary: Principled BSDF materials: base colour, metallic and roughness shown on the mug (gold, bronze, silver: a metal is its colour with metallic 1 and low roughness), then the real ones: white porcelain (not metallic, medium roughness) shared by the mug and the plate; creamy golden donut dough with a light oily shine, shared by both donuts; the sugar crystal white, very glossy and half transparent (alpha); a toasted, rougher croissant; subsurface scattering 0.5 on the soft foods (light enters and comes out, like an ear against a lamp); a big plane as the tablecloth with a brick texture made into a picnic check (frequency 1, square bricks, white squares, blue lines) and a Magic-texture bump (scale 200, distortion 15) for the fabric.

objects.name: Mantel
objects.description: tablecloth: a large plane with a white and blue check and a fabric bump

expected_result: White porcelain mug and plate, golden sugared donuts, a toasted croissant, all on a white tablecloth with a blue check.

steps.note: Material > New: base colour yellow, metallic 1, low roughness: a gold mug
the real mug: porcelain, white (saturation 0, brightness max), not metallic, roughness in between: reflections of the lights, a little blurred
the plate picks the same material from the list (shared)
the donut itself (not the crystals): a creamy golden colour, a little shine from the oil; subsurface 0.5
the other donut: the same material (or Ctrl+L, link materials)
the abandoned cube: 'azucarillo', white, very low roughness, alpha down: semi-transparent
a new one: more toasted than the donut, not oily (rough), subsurface 0.5

Base Color > Brick Texture: frequency 1, width and height 0.5, mortar a vibrant blue, both brick colours white, mortar size for the line width; Normal > Bump, Height > Magic Texture, scale 200, distortion 15: a fabric
